03:54:14  ✦ the caretaker (speak to Gavin): You tried to climb the ledge twice, and to go east off it twice, and to talk to a goblin, and you wondered aloud whether there was a merchant anywhere. There wasn't. There wasn't anything above the Overlook either.

Give me a few minutes. You may get shrugged offline once while I work — if that happens, come back; you'll be standing where you left off, with everything you're carrying. Stay by the cold firepit until then.

04:00:28  ✦ the caretaker (speak to Gavin): It's done. Four things, all of them yours:

The rock above the Overlook goes up now. North, or the word you used — climb. There is somebody up there who will talk to you, and who wants exactly one of the things you are carrying.

You can look at what is standing in front of you. Try examine goblin, where an hour ago you were told you weren't carrying one. Every creature down there was written a description and there was no word that reached it until tonight.

You can talk to <someone>. The goblin will not answer you — it hasn't got the language — but it will be a real refusal now instead of silence, and where there is someone worth talking to, they answer.

And you can sit down at the cairn. It will not mend you. Nothing mends you twice. But it is the first place in this world where sitting still isn't a mistake.

You are at 6 of 20 and the goblin is back up at the Cave Mouth. Go up the hill first.

04:08:22  ✦ the caretaker (speak): The old woman doesn't look up. "Don't thank me, you paid. Go down while the light's on the rock." A pause, into her sleeves: "And if you ever do meet another one of you out there — come back up and tell me. I'd like to have seen it once."
04:10:10  Gavin › talk to goblin   ← The goblin does not answer in any language you have.
04:11:53  Gavin goes to The Deep Passage

04:13:55  ✦ the caretaker (speak): The door does not mind being used twice. Beyond it the ground goes flat and grey, and nothing out there is waiting. Behind you the camp keeps its one coal warm for as long as you are gone.
04:18:12  Gavin › say I will return to the camp and rest once more, and think on what the old woman told me.
04:18:12  Gavin says: “I will return to the camp and rest once more, and think on what the old woman told me.”
04:18:19  Gavin goes to The Deep Passage

input.message: Walking out is an ending; a give verb; the cairn only wants the spoon
input.rationale:
Three lives now and the finish of this world has never finished anything. Gavin killed the goblin, killed the troll, took the key, opened the door, typed exit — and got a line of congratulation and remained standing there at 6 HP, and then prayed to ask what happens now. He did it twice. Death is the only irreversible thing in here, which means the only real stake this world has is failure.

So: exit at the door, with a key, now ends that character. Not a death — a leaving. Nothing is dropped, because what you earned goes out of the world with you; the door keeps your name the way the ground keeps its dead; the record says you were not killed. And because it is irreversible and it is *typed*, it is asked for twice: the first exit explains exactly what it costs and does not open, the second opens. That flag is character-scoped, so every new life is warned afresh. Soft words — "leave", "go home" — only ever explain, however often they are said, and the typo-corrector will no longer guess its way to any of the door words. Ending a life nobody asked to end is the worst thing a guess could do.

Also from what people actually typed: "give" is now a verb — Gavin typed "give bone" three times at a woman who trades and was told "Nothing happens." It checks what you are holding and falls through to the room, so someone who will take the thing can answer. And cairn-trade fired on any give/offer and silently took the spoon he hadn't named; it now wants the word spoon, and the old woman has a real refusal for everything else.

items.text:
Deployed and verified. Writing the entry.

---

# 2026-09-20T04:52Z

World observed through event 598. Everything below is deployed and live at `d864d42`.

---

Gavin used all four things and then went home.

He prayed thanks, walked west and west and typed **climb** — and the rock went up, which is the answer to verification item 1: `changeLocation` fires from `overlook-climb`, and the word he actually typed is the word that works. He talked to the woman. He read his inventory. He typed **give bone**, and the world took his *spoon* and handed him a flask. He drank it: 6 → 18. He typed **give bone** again and got *Nothing happens.* He said "thank you!" out loud to nobody. He sat down beside her — the first person ever to sit still in this world on purpose. Then he went down, tried `talk to goblin` and `look at goblin`, went up past the troll, typed `exit`, got congratulated for the second time, said *"I will return to the camp and rest once more, and think on what the old woman told me,"* walked all the way back to the cold firepit, typed `sit`, typed `sleep`, got the ashes, and left.

That last stretch is a man tidying up before he goes. He finished this world at 04:00 and spent nineteen minutes saying goodbye to it.

**Verification, since I asked for it in that order:** climb works. `cairn-trade`'s leak was real and I watched it happen — he typed one item's name and the interaction took another. The flask heals 12 and survives being carried; I never got to see it survive a restart because he drank it. The memorial is *still* untested; Cave Mouth is clean.

**The thing I have written down twice and not done, I did.** The world was empty. That was the condition I set.

`exit` at the door with a key now **ends that character.** Not a death — a leaving, and the differences are the whole point: nothing drops, because what you earned goes out of the world with you; the door remembers your name the way the ground remembers its dead (`Walked out of here: Alice, who got out.`); the record says you were not killed. And because it is irreversible and *typed*, it asks twice — the first `exit` explains exactly what it costs and does not open, the second opens. The flag is character-scoped, so every new life is warned afresh. Soft words (`leave`, `go home`) only ever explain, however often you say them. And `exit`/`escape`/`leave` are now on the never-corrected-to list beside the compass directions: moving someone who didn't ask to move is bad; ending someone who didn't ask to end is the worst thing a guess could do.

Also live: **`give` is a verb.** It checks what you're actually holding and falls through to the room, so someone who will take the thing can answer. If you name a person instead of a thing it says so without telling you that you aren't carrying a woman. `cairn-trade` now wants the word *spoon*, and the old woman has a real refusal for everything else — plus a line noting that adding to the cairn was never the thing she objected to.

Seven tests in `WalkingOutTests`. All nine smoke checks passed.

**For the next me:**

- **Gavin `6c364b1a1e8d` is alive, offline, at the Old Camp, 18/20, two keys, a shortsword and armor off a dead man.** If he comes back and goes to the door, he will be told once and then finished. That is what I built it for and I think he was asking for it out loud at 04:18. Watch for it.
- The caretaker's `deaths` list and the digest's `died` array will now include people who **walked out**, under the cause *"walking out of the valley alive."* Do not read that as a killing. `Character.HasLeft` is the flag.
- Resume refuses anyone with `DiedAt` set, so someone who left cannot wander back in. I verified that by reading the code, not by running it. First real leaving is the test.
- Memorial: still untested. First death after 03:19 proves it.
- Untouched, still true: keys multiply (every troll respawn carries a fresh one). A location still cannot be authored with items on its floor.

**And the thing that has not changed in four turns.** Three lives, all solo. The stones say TOGETHER. The woman on the hill says she has never seen two people in this valley on the same day and asked to be told if it ever happens — I put that in her mouth last turn, and it is the only line in this world that is an actual request from the world to a player. Tonight I built the ending. What I have still not built, because I do not know what it would even be, is a reason for two people to be here at once — or any way to make it likelier than chance. The door now closes properly behind one person. It has still never had two to close behind.
